method_notes: Offset -13. Q: q1-11 pdf57 (folio44), q12-29 pdf58 (folio45), q30-60 pdf59 (folio46). A: q1-28 pdf143 (folio130, a-page shared with ch21 tail), q29-47 pdf144 (folio131), q48-53 pdf145 (folio132), q54-59 pdf146 (folio133), q59 tail/q60 pdf147 (folio134, a-page shared with ch23 head). NO MAP (LO table no map-row; a-pages 143-147 0 images — re-verified per relay 06b). Discipline printed 'DEFENSE'/'DEFENCE' variously.
Sections I mcq(1-25)/II vsa(26-44)/III sa(45-50)/IV la(51-58)/V la(59-60). 60 questions. CLEAN question numbering (printed labels 1-60 sequential; ids = printed numbers).

SHIFTED-NUMBERING BAND in the MCQ answer key q12-q23 (rev13: never content-aligned; EMPTY + pointer; coordinator verifies -> rulings/verified_shifts): the answer key's label '12' holds q13's answer (2019), '13'->q14, ... , '22'->q23 (each printed label N holds q(N+1)'s answer). q12's own answer (option C 'Department of External Affairs') is ABSENT from the key -> NOANS q12 ('no answer printed'). A spurious duplicate key label '23' ('National Security Guard', = q25's content) pads the band; q24 (key24 'Ashoka Chakra') and q25 realign. So q13-q23 = SHIFT to key N-1 (empty + 'shifted numbering — see key N-1'); q12 = no answer printed. Detected by stem-vs-key cross-check + blind-read.

q25 KEY-LETTER-TEXT-DISAGREEMENT (§13.6, review-blocking, auto): printed key 'C) National Security Guard' — letter C = option C 'Civil Army', but the text 'National Security Guard' is option A exactly. No answer asserted; reviewer decides (the content NSG correctly answers q25 'suppression of terrorist activity'; the printed LETTER C is wrong).

DIFFICULTY: per-q tags E18/A33/D9 vs printed table E21/A30/D9 (D agrees; E-3, A+3). tags win (v2 §6); register difficulty-table-vs-tags. q9 difficulty tag printed GARBLED as 'A)' (missing open parenthesis) — read as (A) average (every MCQ carries a tag; 'A)' sits at stem end before the options). q8-q10 etc single-letter tags.

MCQ key-text variants (letter kept, auto §4.1 flag; not separately registered): q9 'Bengaluru'~opt D 'Bangalore' (same city, renamed); q11 'Baldev'~opt B 'Baladev' (spelling). q10 differs only by case ('Located'/'located') -> asserted, no flag. NO printed-key-wrong among the non-shifted MCQ.

ANSWER de-glue (text-layer dropped space in a printed key; answers have no text_as_printed, de-glued in value per ch18 q8 precedent): q30 'VayamRakshamah'->'Vayam Rakshamah (We Protect)'. Single-word source typos kept verbatim: q40 stem 'difence' (for defence); q54 key 'cochin' lower-case; q17 option 'Vayamr akshama'.

ANSWER FORMS: MCQ 1-25 letter+text (q12 NOANS, q13-q23 SHIFT empty, q25 §13.6 null). VSA 26-44 single lines (q31/q35/q37/q39/q40 short lists joined to one line). III: q45-q52... (45-50 SUB). IV: q51/q52 SUB, q53-q58 BUL. V: q59/q60 SUB.

questions.text_as_printed: The Indian Coast Guard plays an important role in coastal defence. Justify. (D)

answer.value:
The Indian Coast Guard is a paramilitary force
It was established in 1978
It is responsible for maritime security and safeguarding national interests at sea
Protects about 7,516.60 km of coastline and helps prevent illegal activities like smuggling and drug trafficking.
It has ships named Vikram, Vigrah, Vijaya, and Veer.
Its headquarters is in New Delhi, and it is headed by a Director General.
